column2: and another one to deal with

column1: getting the transaction and locking the inodes.
The next couple of patches will need this to be split into two.  One
patch implements committing new parent pointer recordsets to damaged
files.  If one file has an attr fork and the other does not
create the missing attr fork before the atomic swap transaction
use the behavior encoded in the current xfs_bmap_add_attrfork.
The second patch adapts /lost+found adoptions to handle parent pointers
correctly.  The adoption process will add a parent pointer to a child
that is being moved to /lost+found
column2: but this requires that the attr fork

column1: already exists.  We don't know if we're actually going to commit the
adoption until we've already reserved a transaction and taken the
ILOCKs
column2: which means that we must have a way to bypass the start of the

column1: current xfs_bmap_add_attrfork.
Therefore
column2: create xfs_attr_add_fork as the helper that creates a

column1: transaction and takes locks; and make xfs_bmap_add_attrfork the function
that updates the inode core and allocates the incore attr fork.
